pl-l3d40c1-d1e115.summary: Gives the sixth precept of the second tablet: you shall not desire your neighbor's wife.

pl-l3d40c1-d1e121.summary: Gives the seventh: you shall not covet your neighbor's house, his servant, his maid, and so on.

pl-l3d40c1-d1e127.summary: Notes that the precept against coveting a neighbor's goods seems the same as 'you shall not steal', and that against coveting his wife the same as 'you shall not commit adultery'. But those two forbid the deeds, these the concupiscence itself, so they differ much. Hence the Gospel adds to the precept against adultery, forbidding all desire for it.
claims: The last two precepts forbid desire, the earlier ones the deed.
The Gospel extends the prohibition of adultery to desire.

pl-l3d40c1-d1e146.summary: Asks why, if the Law forbids coveting another's wife and goods, the Law is said to restrain the hand and not the mind, but the Gospel both hand and mind.

pl-l3d40c1-d1e149.summary: Answers that this is said of the Law regarding its ceremonial, not moral, precepts; or because the Law lacks a general prohibition of all deadly concupiscence, as in the Gospel.
claims: The Law restrains only the hand in its ceremonial precepts.
The Law lacks a general prohibition of deadly concupiscence.

pl-l3d40c1.summary: Gives the last two precepts: not coveting the neighbor's wife and not coveting his house, servants, and goods. They might seem identical with the precepts against adultery and theft, but those forbid the deeds, these the desire itself, so they differ greatly; and the Gospel adds to the precept against adultery by forbidding all desire for it. Asked why the Law is said to restrain the hand and not the mind, while the Gospel restrains both, Lombard answers that this refers to the ceremonial, not the moral, precepts, or that the Law lacks a general prohibition of all deadly concupiscence as the Gospel has.
claims: The last two precepts forbid desire, while those against adultery and theft forbid deeds.
The Law restrains the hand with respect to its ceremonial precepts.
The Gospel contains a general prohibition of deadly concupiscence.
